title: Independent coupling preserving polynomial distributions
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $F$ assign a real coefficient to every subset of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,
u)$ be probability spaces, and let $X_i:\Omega	o\mathbb R$ and $Y_i:\Xi	o\mathbb R$ be measurable up to null sets. Suppose the family $(X_i)_{i<n}$ is mutually independent under $\mu$, and $(Y_i)_{i<n}$ is mutually independent under $
u$. There exist a probability space carrying a mutually independent family $(Z_j)_{j\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)\sqcup\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ whose left and right coordinates have the respective distributions of $X_i$ and $Y_i$, and such that evaluating $F$ on each coordinate family gives, respectively, the same distributions as evaluating it on $X$ under $\mu$ and on $Y$ under $
u$.
hypotheses_covered: Coefficient family $F$ on subsets of the $n$ coordinates
Each $X_i$ is measurable up to $\mu$-null sets
Each $Y_i$ is measurable up to $\nu$-null sets
